source.title: MicroEdit: Neuron-level Knowledge Disentanglement and Localization in Lifelong Model Editing
source.authors: Shiqi Wang; Qi Wang; Run-Liang Niu; He Kong; Yi Chang

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses an SAE to localize and edit representations, relying on sparse features to reduce semantic entanglement, but does not test the claim’s neuron-job audit or explanation-evaluation versions.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates knowledge-editing performance, not the share of neuron poles with one or more jobs, held-out explanation prediction, automated explanation scores, or attribution graphs built from a model’s neurons. Those editing results do not test the listed versions. Section 2 reports an activation-overlap analysis; the stated maximum is recorded below, but it does not measure the claimed job-share or explanation accuracy.
record.test_reason: This is a lifelong knowledge-editing method paper (MicroEdit) that uses a pretrained SAE and reports editing performance. It assumes neurons are polysemantic, citing Bricken 2023 and Elhage 2022. It never audits neuron jobs, scores explanations, tests canonical polysemantic neurons, compares interpretability across architectures or tools, or builds neuron attribution graphs. Its one interpretability-flavoured measure, activation overlap between 10 statements, does not show whether a neuron has one job or several.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors argue that knowledge entanglement during editing stems from neuron polysemanticity. They say SAE-based sparse decoder updates with a reconstruction-distance switch reduce interference and outperform baselines in lifelong editing on LLaMA-3-8B and Mistral-7B. Appendix A.3 also attributes degradation at 10K edits to polysemy they call nearly unavoidable, which is an interpretation, not a measurement.
record.recipe_differences: No neuron-job audit or explanation-evaluation recipe is applied; the paper uses an SAE-based method for lifelong knowledge editing.

fits_no_version.finding: Semantically unrelated knowledge statements, e.g. bananas/potassium versus geocentric Sun, share up to 18% of activated neurons in an unnamed LLM, over 10 randomly chosen statements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unrelated factual statements partly share activated neurons in LLMs. The authors read this as polysemantic entanglement that interferes with editing.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The activation-overlap analysis covers 10 randomly selected statements; the stated maximum is not assigned to either of the two token-aggregation methods in the text. It does not evaluate neuron explanations on held-out activations.
record.rows_left_out: Editing-performance tables, editing ablations, layer and hyperparameter sweeps, and cited findings were left out because they do not measure the listed claim versions or the job interpretability claim.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or of job shares.
No job-share measurement across models, scales or dense versus MoE models. LLaMA-3-8B and Mistral-7B are used only for editing.
No vision models, no InceptionV1 cat/car neuron, no pose or recursive-generalization analysis.
No measure of how the interpretable-neuron share varies with architecture, regularization or tools.
No attribution graphs from native neurons and no comparison with replacement-model reconstruction error.
No test of whether explanations from activating examples predict held-out firing.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The paper assumes the opposite of the essay's thesis: that neurons are polysemantic. It offers only a weak overlap statistic, with no explanation or job analysis, so it cannot challenge V1 or V2. Editing tables, ablations and sweeps were rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit the proportion of neuron poles with one main job, two related jobs, or jobs not understood.
Does not measure job shares across models or scales, or compare dense and mixture-of-experts models.
Does not study InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose detection, or recursive generalization.
Does not estimate how interpretability shares vary with architecture, regularization, tools, or vision-model size.
Does not test whether attribution graphs made from a model’s own neurons explain behavior or compare them with a replacement model.
Does not test explanations against held-out activating examples or measure where neurons fire.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: LLM (model not specified for this analysis)
rows.operation_detail: Compared neuron activation similarities across 10 randomly selected knowledge statements.

conditions.value: 10 randomly selected statements; the text gives bananas containing potassium and the Sun revolving around Earth in geocentric models as an unrelated pair
The analysis reports averages across all tokens and separately using only the last token; the text does not assign the stated maximum to either

rows.measure: Overlap in activated neurons between knowledge statements
rows.note: The text reports this maximum for semantically unrelated knowledge pairs but does not identify which aggregation produced it. This is an activation-overlap result, not a count of neuron jobs or an explanation test.
rows.check: The model is unnamed for this analysis, as is which 'neurons' (residual, MLP or other) and what activation threshold define overlap. It is also unclear which aggregation, all tokens or last token, gives the 18% maximum. A shared-activation fraction across two sentences cannot show whether a neuron pole has one main job or several related ones. 'Observed' has no meaning against any version, so it is set to cannot_determine.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
